# GALA

> GALA is a statically-typed, functional-first language that transpiles to Go. It has sealed types with exhaustive pattern matching, `Option`/`Try`/`Either` instead of `nil` and naked error pairs, immutability by default, and full Go interop. Source files are `.gala`; the compiler is `gala`.

GALA is close enough to Scala and Kotlin to be readable on sight, and different enough in specific places to trip a model writing from memory. The differences are listed below, with the compiler error each mistake produces. Every one of them is a hard compile error, not a lint — the build stops and names the fix.

## Getting the compiler to tell you

- `gala build ./main.gala` — compile; diagnostics carry a stable `GALA-Exxxx` code, a source span, and a fix hint
- `gala build --json ./main.gala` — the same diagnostics as JSON (`code`, `message`, `hint`, `file`, `line`, `column`, `endColumn`, `docsUrl`). Prefer this over parsing the framed text output
- `gala explain GALA-E0044` — the full reference page for a code, offline; `gala explain --list` enumerates them
- `gala run ./main.gala`, `gala test ./...`
- `gala doctor --json` — checks Go, the Go SDK used for type inference, gala's caches and the project's `gala.mod`/`go.mod`; each problem has a `fix` and a `docsUrl` into [Troubleshooting](https://gala.fyi/docs/troubleshooting/). Run it first when a build fails for no reason in the code

## Differences that most often produce wrong code

- **Lambda parameters are always parenthesized.** `(x) => x * 2`, never `x => x * 2`. Applies to one parameter too. (`GALA-E0042`)
- **`match` is postfix.** `value match { case ... }`, not Rust's `match value { ... }`.
- **Methods are capitalized.** `.Map`, `.Filter`, `.Size` — not `.map`/`.filter`. `map` is additionally a reserved keyword, so `.map` fails in the parser.
- **Collections are built by named functions, never by calling the type.** `ArrayOf(1, 2, 3)`, `ListOf(...)`, `HashMapOf(("a", 1))`, `EmptyHashMap[K, V]()`. Scala's `List(1, 2, 3)` is an error. (`GALA-E0043`)
- **There is no `->` pair arrow.** A map entry is a tuple: `HashMapOf(("a", 1), ("b", 2))`.
- **No bare `len`, `append`, `make`, `panic`, `recover`.** Use `.Size()` (runes/elements) or `.ByteSize()` (bytes). (`GALA-E0035`)
- **No `defer`, no bare `go`.** Cleanup is `use` or `Using(res, (r) => ...)`; a goroutine is `go_interop.Spawn(() => f())`. (`GALA-E0036`)
- **`use` binds the resource, not a `Try`.** `use f = os.Open(p)` is an error, because `os.Open` gives a `Try[*os.File]`; write `use f = os.Open(p).Get()` inside `Try(() => { ... })`. (`GALA-E0118`)
- **No `//go:` directives in a `.gala` file.** `//go:embed` is `embed val content = "file.txt"`; a `//go:build` constraint stays in a hand-written `.go` file of the package. (`GALA-E0119`)
- **No slice or map literals**, and Go slice/map *types* are legal only where a type is expected. (`GALA-E0007`, `GALA-E0008`, `GALA-E0040`)
- **No struct tags.** ``Name string `json:"name"` `` is an error (`GALA-E0085`). JSON and YAML keys are set on the codec: `Codec[User](SnakeCase()).Rename("Name", "full_name").OmitEmpty("Bio")`. A type that a Go library must read through tags goes in a hand-written `.go` file of the same package.
- **No Go function literals.** A function value is a lambda: `(x int) int => { ... }`, never `func(x int) int { ... }`; an unnamed Go parameter is written `_ T`, and the body carries over. (`GALA-E0117`)
- **No `const`, no declaration groups.** A constant is a `val` (`val MaxRetries = 3`); declare one name per `val`/`var`/`type`, never `var ( ... )`; an `iota` enumeration is a `sealed type`. (`GALA-E0121`, `GALA-E0122`)
- **No `switch`, no type assertions.** `switch x { case 1, 2: ... default: ... }` is `x match { case 1 | 2 => ... case _ => ... }`; a tagless switch is an `if` / `else if` chain; `x.(T)` and type switches are `x match { case v: T => ... case _ => ... }`. (`GALA-E0123`, `GALA-E0124`)
- **One result value, no result names.** `return a, b` is `return (a, b)` for a Go result list `(A, B)`, and `return Success(v)` / `return Failure(err)` for `(T, error)`; named results `(n int, err error)` are written as types alone. (`GALA-E0132`, `GALA-E0130`)
- **Go type forms that GALA does not spell.** `interface{}` is `any`; a fixed-size array `[16]byte` is a slice or an `Array`; a struct names every field (`Base Base`, no embedding) and an interface lists its methods; type-set constraints (`~int | ~float64`) come from Go (`cmp.Ordered`) or a `.go` file; each type parameter has its own constraint, `[K any, V any]`. (`GALA-E0125`, `GALA-E0126`, `GALA-E0127`, `GALA-E0131`)
- **No slice expressions, no labels.** `s[1:3]`, `s[1:]`, `s[:2]` are `.Slice(1, 3)`, `.Drop(1)`, `.Take(2)` on an `Array`/`List`, or `go_interop.Slice`/`SliceDrop`/`SliceTake` on a Go slice; `break outer` / `continue outer` have no form: use a flag `var` or a function and `return`. (`GALA-E0128`, `GALA-E0129`)
- **No `make`, `min`, `max`, `clear`.** `make([]T, n)` is `go_interop.SliceWithSize[T](n)`, `make(map[K]V)` is `go_interop.MapEmpty[K, V]()`; `min(a, b)` is `if (a < b) a else b` or `math.Min`. (`GALA-E0035`)
- **Every import must be used.** An import nothing in the file refers to is an error, as in Go; std is always available, so never write `import . "martianoff/gala/std"` without using a std name. Write `import _ "path"` to import a package only for its initialization. (`GALA-E0120`)
- **No named `func` inside a function body.** A local helper is a lambda bound to a `val`: `val helper = (x int) int => x + 1`; for recursion, `var fact func(int) int` then assign. (`GALA-E0052`)
- **A type alias has no `=`.** `type Result[T any] Either[AppError, T]`, not Go's `type Result[T any] = Either[AppError, T]` (a parse error). An alias is the same type as its target, not a new type; a generic alias takes no methods, and a type that needs an identity or methods of its own is a struct. (`GALA-E0048`)
- **`val` is immutable and is the default.** Use `var` only when reassignment is genuinely needed.
- **Parameters, lambda parameters and receivers are immutable.** Reassigning `n` in `func f(n int)` or `(n) => ...` is an error; write `var n` to allow it. A receiver can never be rebound (no `var` receiver): copy it into a local `var`. Writing its `var` fields through it is fine.
- **No `val _ = expr`.** To drop a value, write the expression as a bare statement; in a lambda with no result, an `error`-only call becomes `FromError(call())`. (`GALA-E0060`)
- **Several values in one arm are alternatives, not Go's `case 1, 2:`.** Write `case 1 | 2 =>` or `case Some("a" | "b") =>`; `|` in a pattern is never a bitwise OR. Alternatives bind no names, so use `_` inside them. (`GALA-E0071`)
- **Sealed matches must be exhaustive.** Adding a variant turns every incomplete match site into a compile error naming the missing case — this is the property to lean on when refactoring. (`GALA-E0002`) Test a variant with `match`, not `isCircle()`: those predicates are private to the sealed type's package (`GALA-E0083` from another one).
- **`==` is `Equal`, not Go's `==`.** On a struct, sealed type, tuple, `Option` or collection, `a == b` is `a.Equal(b)`: two Lists built separately with the same elements are `==`. On a `T comparable`, `a == b` compares by `Equal` too, and so does `==` on a Go type with `Equal(T) bool` such as `time.Time`. Pointers, interfaces and other Go types keep Go's `==`. A function, a Go slice or map, and a `T any` cannot be compared (`GALA-E0084`).
- **Prefer `Option`/`Try`/`Either` over `nil` and `(T, error)`.** Pattern-match to extract; do not call `.Get()` without checking. For a call (Go or GALA) returning only `error`, `Try(call)` (or `FromError(call)`) is a `Try[Void]` that fails on a non-nil error.
- **`&x` is a `Ptr[T]`, a pointer that is never nil.** It passes as a `*T`, but `nil` or a Go `*T` never fills a `Ptr` and `p == nil` on one is an error (`GALA-E0080`). Turn a Go pointer into one with `RequirePtr(p)`, or into an `OptionPtr[T]` (a pointer that may be absent) with `OptionPtrOf(p)`; a `var` that later takes a Go pointer or `nil` is declared `var p *T = &x`. Match an `OptionPtr` directly with `case Some(p)` / `case None()`; no `.ToOption()` is needed.
- **To change a caller's value, use an `inout` parameter, and mark the argument with `&`.** `func bump(inout c Counter)` is called `bump(&c)` on a `var` (a missing `&` is `GALA-E0111`); an `inout` receiver `func (inout c Counter) inc()` is called `c.inc()` on a `var`, not a `val` (`GALA-E0114`). The callee may not keep the place: no capturing it in a lambda, even one passed to `ForEach`, and no passing it to Go (`GALA-E0113`).
- **A Go call returning `(T, error)` is a `Try[T]`, not a `T`.** `val n = strconv.Atoi(s)` makes `n` a `Try[int]`; using it as an `int` is an error. Use `match { case Success(v) => ... case Failure(e) => ... }`, `.GetOrElse(default)`, `.Map(...)`, or `.Get()` (panics on failure); or bind Go-style with `val v, err = strconv.Atoi(s)`. Don't wrap it in `Try(...)` — that is the same `Try[int]`. A Go call returning `(A, B)` or more values is a Tuple: `val (k, v, found) = strings.Cut(s, "=")`. (`GALA-E0049`)
- **A function Go calls with several results declares Go's result list.** `func (c *Counter) Write(p []byte) (int, error)` implements `io.Writer`; its body gives a `Try[int]` (`Success(n)` or `Failure(err)`), and an `(A, B)` list takes a Tuple. A lambda passed as a Go `func() (T, error)` callback likewise gives a `Try`. A failed `Try` gives Go the zero value; where the value matters with its error (an `io.Reader` returning `n > 0` with `io.EOF`, a short write) give `ResultsOf(goCall(...))` from `go_interop`, a `Tuple[T, error]` Go receives as it is. A body value of another type is `GALA-E0134`.
- **A codec decodes a struct with an unexported (lowercase) field only through `func (x T) Validate() Try[T]`.** `json.Codec[T]` / `yaml.Codec[T]` over such a struct — as the root, a field, or inside a collection — needs that exact method, which may simply return `Success(x)`; a codec over a struct of exported fields needs nothing. (`GALA-E0050`, `GALA-E0057`)
- **`type X Y` is an alias, not a newtype.** `X` and `Y` are one type, so a `Y` passes for an `X`, and `X` takes a method only when `Y` is a plain type (or a pointer to one) declared in the same package. For a distinct type with methods, declare `opaque type UserID int64`; the codec still writes it as the bare value. (`GALA-E0048`)
- **An `opaque type` never converts implicitly, and does not encapsulate.** Write `UserID(n)` and `int64(id)` explicitly (passing an `int64` for a `UserID` is `GALA-E0064`; `OrderID(userID)` is `GALA-E0063`, write `OrderID(int64(userID))`); untyped constants such as `42` still mix. Any package can convert, so a value that must be validated is `struct Email(v string)` with a constructor, not an opaque type. Its methods are not inherited from the underlying type: `opaque type Wait time.Duration` has no `.Seconds()`.
- **Implement an interface inline with an interface literal, not a one-off struct.** `UserRepo(Find = (id) => None(), Count = () => 0)` gives every method by name, with lambda types taken from the interface; Go interfaces work too, `fmt.Stringer(String = () => "x")`. Leaving out a method is `GALA-E0078`. Dependencies are constructor parameters faked this way in tests; there is no DI container or implicit parameter.
- **An interface method takes no type parameters of its own.** Scala's `def map[U](f: T => U): U` in a trait has no GALA interface form: `Map[U any](...)` in an `interface` is `GALA-E0086`. Put the type parameter on the interface (`type Box[T any] interface { ... }`), or write a generic function that takes the interface value. Methods of a struct may declare type parameters.
- **`case UserID(n)` unwraps exactly one value.** `n` is the underlying `int64`; `case UserID(a, b)` or `case UserID()` is `GALA-E0065`. An opaque type is not sealed, so a match on one ends in `case _`; a phantom-typed one matched on `any` spells its type arguments, `case Id[User](n)`.

## Go habits, and their GALA form

Some Go forms compile in a `.gala` file, so the build will not stop you; write the GALA form anyway. The others are the compile errors named.

- **`x := v` → `val x = v`.** `:=` compiles, but it declares an immutable binding (reassigning it is an error); write `val`, or `var x = v` when it must change.
- **C-style `for i := 0; i < n; i++` and `for _, x := range xs` → collection methods.** `range` over a GALA `Array`, `List`, `HashMap` or other GALA struct does not compile (`GALA-E0133`); over a Go slice, array, map, string, integer, channel or function, and the C-style loop, it compiles but is still a Go habit. Write `xs.Map(f)`, `xs.Filter(p)`, `xs.ForEach(f)`, `xs.FoldLeft(z, f)`, and `xs.ZipWithIndex()` when the index matters.
- **`if v, err := f(); err != nil` → `match` on the `Try`.** `if` takes no initializer (`GALA-E0047`).
- **`v, err := f()` then `if err != nil` → the `Try`.** It compiles and gives Go's raw values, but a Go `(T, error)` call already is a `Try[T]`: `f() match { case Success(v) => ... case Failure(e) => ... }`, `.Map(...)`, `.GetOrElse(d)`, or a `bind` block. A call that returns only `error` is `FromError(call)`, a `Try[Void]`.
- **`fmt.Println(a, b)` → `Println(a, b)`; `fmt.Sprintf("%d items", n)` → `s"$n items"`**, and `f"$price%.2f"` for a format verb. Both `fmt` forms compile; the GALA forms are built in and need no import. Keep `fmt` for `fmt.Errorf` and `fmt.Fprintf`.
- **`if p == nil` and `return nil` → `Option[T]`.** Go pointers and `nil` compile, but a GALA function returns `Some(v)` / `None()` and the caller `match`es on it; a Go pointer that may be nil becomes `OptionPtrOf(p)` at the boundary.
- **`defer f.Close()` → `use f = ...`.** (`GALA-E0036`)
- **Goroutines and channels → `Future`.** `go f()` is `GALA-E0036` and `chan T` is `GALA-E0055`. Fan-out and collect is `Traverse(items, (x) => Future(work(x))).Await()` from `concurrent`, a `Try[Array[R]]`; `go_interop.Spawn` is only for fire-and-forget work.
- **`append` → collection operations.** Bare `append` is `GALA-E0035`. Build with `xs.Append(x)`, `Map`, `Filter` or `FoldLeft` on an `Array`/`List`; `go_interop.SliceAppend` is for a Go slice at the boundary.

## Shape of a program

```gala
package main

import . "martianoff/gala/collection_immutable"

sealed type Shape {
    case Circle(R float64)
    case Square(S float64)
}

func area(s Shape) float64 = s match {
    case Circle(r) => 3.14 * r * r
    case Square(a) => a * a
}

func main() {
    val shapes = ArrayOf(Circle(1.0), Square(2.0))
    val total = shapes.Map((s) => area(s)).FoldLeft(0.0, (acc, x) => acc + x)
    Println(s"total = ${total}")
}
```

`Println` and string interpolation (`s"..."`, `f"...%0.2f"`) are built in — no `fmt` import needed.

## Docs

- [Language reference](https://gala.fyi/docs/language-reference/): full syntax and semantics
- [Error codes](https://gala.fyi/docs/errors/): every `GALA-Exxxx`, with a repro, the real compiler output, and the fix
- [Examples](https://gala.fyi/docs/examples/): feature-by-feature programs
- [Immutable collections](https://gala.fyi/docs/immutable-collections/) · [Mutable collections](https://gala.fyi/docs/mutable-collections/): the method surface
- [Go interop](https://gala.fyi/features/go-interop/): calling Go, and where Go types are allowed
- [Ownership](https://gala.fyi/docs/ownership/): `inout` parameters, which lend a caller's place for one call; the rules the compiler checks (`GALA-E0111` to `GALA-E0116`) and their fixes, Go interop, interfaces
- [Go interop guide](https://gala.fyi/docs/go-interop/): mixing GALA and Go in both directions, mixed packages, building, using GALA from plain Go modules (`go.gala.fyi/stdlib`, `gala export`, `gala transpile --stdlib-module`), gotchas
- [Add GALA to a Go repository](https://gala.fyi/docs/add-gala-to-go-repo/): `gala mod init` in an existing Go module, `.gala` files beside `.go` files in one package, calls both ways, Go dependencies in `gala.mod`, and a cobra CLI written in GALA
- [Porting from Go](https://gala.fyi/docs/porting-from-go/): every Go construct mapped to its GALA form, or to `go_interop`, `Codec[T]` or a hand-written `.go` file, with the error code the Go form gets: `switch`, `(T, error)`, `defer`, `panic`, slices and maps, struct tags, `const`, goroutines, channels and `select`
- [Dependency injection](https://gala.fyi/docs/dependency-injection/): explicit wiring through constructor parameters, and test fakes built with interface literals
- [Pattern matching](https://gala.fyi/features/pattern-matching/) · [Sealed types](https://gala.fyi/features/sealed-types/)
- [For AI agents](https://gala.fyi/for-ai/): why the compiler suits a generate-check-fix loop
